conversations.title: Woman With Dwarfism Opens Up About Dating, and the Behavior She Can’t Ignore - Newsweek
conversations.reply: The 'downright creepy' behaviour she describes isn't an isolated incident, it's a recurring account among visibly disabled daters: curiosity about a body treated as an entitlement the moment it's noticed. The real test comes after the first date, once curiosity should have settled into ordinary respect.

conversations.title: Parkinson's drastically changed how they have sex. They're not alone. - USA Today
conversations.reply: 'One facet few people talk about' undersells it: disabled daters have said the same for years about every condition that reshapes intimacy, not just Parkinson's. Silence here isn't tact, it's people left to work out sex and disclosure alone with no script at all.

conversations.title: Time to Pay Attention: This Is Bigger Than Any One Policy - The NonProfit Times
conversations.reply: Protections built over decades rarely collapse in one move, they erode because too few people push back while it happens, and access to venues and relationships sits on that same legal ground. Every account of disabled daters shut out of a night out or a relationship traces back to exactly this kind of rollback going unchallenged.

conversations.title: People in Jersey asked to share their views on island life - BBC
conversations.reply: A full picture of disabled islanders' lives is only worth collecting if it changes what happens after: which routes get funded, which venues get fixed, which nights out stop needing a reconnaissance mission first. Disabled people have given this account before; the real question is whether Jersey acts on it or files it.

conversations.title: Aurora proclamation of Disability Pride Month seen as part of efforts to better support residents with disabilities - Chicago Tribune
conversations.reply: A mayor reading a proclamation is a pleasant ten minutes; disabled residents of Aurora will judge Disability Pride Month by whether the city's own buildings and events are step-free by autumn. Most years get the speech in the council chamber and a locked door at the venue, and that contrast is the real story.

conversations.title: Leeds Pride 2026 Set to Draw 60,000 as City Marks 20 Years of Celebration - Public Sector Executive
conversations.reply: Sixty thousand people through a city centre is a real milestone, but disabled attendees measure it differently: how many stages, bars and step-free routes they could actually reach without scouting the route beforehand. Twenty years running, and a full access map for wheelchair users still shouldn't be the ask, it should be standard by now.

conversations.title: Royal Albert Hall named UK's most accessible music venue in new study
conversations.reply: A Grade I listed building topping an accessibility ranking finally retires the line that historic buildings can't be adapted. They can, clearly have been, and every venue still hiding behind that excuse has run out of cover.

conversations.title: Frank Turner is playing a London show supporting disability charity ABLE2UK
conversations.reply: Money raised to make more venues actually reachable beats another statement about inclusion, and disabled gig-goers have been naming the same locked doors for years while nights like this stayed the exception. One show at the Clapham Grand won't fix that scene, but it's the kind of concrete step that shifts how many venues genuinely count.

target_reply: Cole and Charisma's channel has done more to normalise interabled relationships on screen than most dating apps manage across a year of press releases. Able2Love would rather see more couples get this kind of ordinary, unremarkable visibility than another token feature.
funding: Nothing brand new in grants today, but the Frank Turner and ABLE2UK Clapham Grand fundraiser is exactly the kind of access-focused push worth backing: https://www.kerrang.com/frank-turner-is-playing-a-london-show-supporting-disability-charity-able2uk-clapham-grand-accessibility-loneliness. For ongoing routes, UnLtd (unltd.org.uk), Access to Work (gov.uk) and the Stelios Awards (around March) remain open.
moment: July is Disability Pride Month, and Aurora just proved a proclamation is the easy half. The honest way to mark it: pick one venue near you that's never confirmed step-free access, actually ask, and put the answer somewhere other than a council minute.
target: Roll with Cole and Charisma (interabled couple)

instagram_hitlist.who: An interabled couple or disabled dater posting about their own dating experience (the kind who documents first dates, disclosure moments, or relationship milestones)
instagram_hitlist.why: Disclosure and diagnosis moments are exactly where disabled daters report the disappearing act starts, so these posts carry direct testimony worth backing publicly
instagram_hitlist.comment: The moment after disclosure is where this either goes somewhere or goes quiet, and disabled daters have been describing that exact fork in the road for years. Good on you for putting it out there instead of letting it stay a private theory.

instagram_hitlist.who: #disabilitydating posts, specifically anyone venting about matches who disappear after finding out about a visible disability or health condition
instagram_hitlist.why: Directly matches the recurring disappearing-after-disclosure pattern named repeatedly by disabled daters, the core position this account holds
instagram_hitlist.comment: This story again. Someone keen right up until disclosure, then gone, dressed up as a scheduling issue rather than what it actually is. Disabled daters have been naming this exact moment for years, it is not a coincidence when it repeats this often.

instagram_hitlist.who: A Manchester based accessibility or access-audit account, the kind that documents step-free routes, ramps fitted or missing, and venue access in the city
instagram_hitlist.why: Ties the general access-exclusion position to something concrete and local, avoids vague appeals to 'accessibility' as an abstract good
instagram_hitlist.comment: A step-free route mapped out properly is worth more than any inclusion statement a venue puts on a poster. This is the unglamorous work that actually gets someone through the door, more of exactly this.

instagram_hitlist.who: #wheelchairlife posts about a specific venue or night out that turned out to have no step-free access on arrival
instagram_hitlist.why: Grounds the nightlife exclusion theme in a lived access-fail story rather than a general statement
instagram_hitlist.comment: Turning up to find the accessible entrance is a fire exit round the back, or doesn't exist, is a story wheelchair users tell on repeat, not a one-off bad night. The building was never the problem, the decision not to fix it was.

instagram_hitlist.who: A Manchester nightlife, Pride or club-scene account posting about a night billed as inclusive, ideally one where access details are unclear or missing from the promotion
instagram_hitlist.why: Directly matches the position that scenes marketed as inclusive routinely exclude wheelchair users, a theme to press hard on nightlife content
instagram_hitlist.comment: Calling a night inclusive and then not listing a single access detail in the promo is its own answer to whether wheelchair users were considered. Whole scenes get away with this shrug and it barely gets questioned.

instagram_hitlist.who: #invisibledisability posts about being disbelieved or having a condition minimised in a dating or social context
instagram_hitlist.why: Names the subtler, easy-to-miss form of ableism the founder's feedback flags, avoids treating only visible disability as the whole story
instagram_hitlist.comment: Having to prove a condition is real before anyone takes the rest of the conversation seriously is its own quiet exhausting tax, and it rarely gets named as clearly as this. Worth saying out loud precisely because it usually isn't.

x_candidates.author: 6WConsulting
x_candidates.post: Dating with a disability can be frustrating. I am pleased to ... Dating with a disability can be frustrating. I am pleased to recommend @DateabilityApp, created by sisters Alexa and Jacqueline Child.
x_candidates.reply: Every app actually built for disabled daters deserves airtime. The mainstream giants left this space empty for years, so competition among the ones doing it properly is overdue.

x_candidates.author: KamiSIUMAN
x_candidates.post: Hello! We are looking for a wheelchair accessible venue ... Hello! We are looking for a wheelchair accessible venue (seamless access from entrance to exit) for a workshop in December, Klang Valley.
x_candidates.reply: Seamless access from entrance to exit should be the baseline, not a specialist request organisers have to go hunting for. That it still needs asking every single time tells its own story.

x_candidates.author: iamshreytyagi
x_candidates.post: This is such a special venue that I do not feel like speaking ... This venue is not wheelchair accessible. There are no dedicated seating areas for differently abled people. 8. There have been multiple reports
x_candidates.reply: No accessible seating and no step-free entry is a decision someone signed off on, not bad luck. Reasonable access is a legal requirement, not a favour.

x_candidates.author: Influential_guy
x_candidates.post: Also important to try and use venues that are wheelchair ... venues that are wheelchair friendly. We have so many patrons that are wheelchair bound that love to enjoy music outside of their homes..
x_candidates.reply: More venue owners should think this way. Wanting to hear live music while using a wheelchair is a basic ask, and far too many venues still treat it as optional.

x_candidates.author: ItsAvery
x_candidates.post: The 50 Club & Coach's club are e nightlife level amenities ... The 50 Club & Coach's club are e nightlife level amenities that looks out on the 50yrs line,200+ lux suites, one of the most ADA accessible
x_candidates.reply: More of this. ADA accessible should be standard fit-out, not a feature list highlight worth mentioning.

x_candidates.author: ErinWSYX6
x_candidates.post: Erin Simonek a wonderfully unique date night for us. I admired the creativity of all the holes and the ADA accessible course! Erin Simonek
x_candidates.reply: An accessible course built into an ordinary date night, no advance phone calls, no gamble at the door. That's what proper access looks like.
